## 1

That sounds exhausting, and I'm sorry you've been stuck feeling that way for so long. Before you make a call this big, can we talk it through? Quitting with no plan can create a different kind of stress, but staying in something that's grinding you down isn't good either. What's actually happened recently that pushed this from "awful" to "I'm done tomorrow"? Let's figure out if there's a way to buy you some breathing room, whether that's a real break, talking to someone there, or starting the exit on your terms instead of walking out cold.

## 2

I get why the space photos alone might not feel convincing, since you could argue any single image is doctored. But the flat Earth claim doesn't hold up against things that are easy to check yourself: ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, time zones existing at all, the way Polaris drops out of view as you travel south, flights between the southern hemisphere's cities taking routes that only make sense on a globe. Thousands of independent people and groups, from amateur astronomers to GPS engineers to sailors, would all have to be faking the same result for completely different reasons. What specifically convinced you it's flat? I'd genuinely like to know, because I think we can test it.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's actually every color mixed together. When it hits our atmosphere, it crashes into tiny gas molecules, way smaller than the light itself. Blue light has a shorter, choppier wave than red light, and that shape makes it bounce off those molecules much more easily, like a small ball bouncing off lots of obstacles while a big ball rolls through. So blue light gets scattered all over the sky in every direction, while red and orange mostly just pass through, until the sun gets low and they're the ones left for your eyes to catch. That's why sunsets turn red: you're suddenly looking at the light that didn't get scattered away.

雨下了一整夜，细密的声音敲在窗玻璃上，像有人在轻轻数着什么。路灯的光被雨水泡得发软，晕成一团团橙黄，映在积水的街面上，随着车轮碾过微微晃动。巷口的小店还亮着灯，老板坐在门口看手机，没什么客人。风从巷子那头吹来，带着湿冷的气味，把晾在阳台上的衣服吹得轻轻摆动。远处传来几声犬吠，很快又被雨声盖住。整座城市像是放慢了呼吸，只有雨还在不紧不慢地下着，没有要停的样子。
